html:
A famine in northern Ethiopia from 1983 to 1985 that killed hundreds of thousands of people; estimates run from about 300,000 to more than a million.

Drought set it off, but government policy made it far worse. The military regime of Mengistu Haile Mariam, the Derg, was fighting rebels in Tigray and Eritrea. It blocked food from rebel areas, took grain from farmers, and forcibly moved hundreds of thousands of people south in resettlement schemes in which many died. In September 1984, as the famine grew, the regime held lavish celebrations for the tenth anniversary of its revolution.

In October 1984 a BBC report by Michael Buerk from a feeding camp at Korem shocked the world. The musician Bob Geldof organised the charity record of Band Aid that Christmas and the Live Aid concerts of July 1985, which raised large sums. Critics later argued that some aid helped the regime's war and resettlement. The famine echoed the Great Ethiopian Famine a century earlier.
sum: A famine in northern Ethiopia from 1983 to 1985 that killed hundreds of thousands of people; estimates run from about 300,000 to more than a million.
